934.summary: The class explores the opening of the Gospel of Mark, focusing on the baptism of Jesus and the divine affirmation of his identity as the Son of God. It emphasizes the significance of Jesus' baptism and the anointing of the Holy Spirit upon him.

935.summary: The class explores the authority of Jesus Christ in the Gospel of Mark, focusing on his baptism, wilderness temptation, and calling of the first disciples. It emphasizes Jesus' humanity and the divine mission he undertakes, contrasting his experiences with those of Adam and the disciples' willingness to leave their livelihoods for his service.

936.summary: The class discusses Jesus' early morning prayer after healing many people, emphasizing the importance of prayer and early devotion to God. It also covers Jesus' mission to preach and heal, highlighting his role as the Son of Man with divine authority.

937.summary: The class discusses Jesus' authority to forgive sins and his call to Levi (Matthew) to follow him, emphasizing Jesus' understanding of the scriptures and his compassion for those in need. It also covers Jesus' confrontation with the Pharisees over the Sabbath and his healing of a man with a withered hand.

938.summary: The class discusses the founding of the Ecclesia in the Gospel of Mark, focusing on Jesus' call of the twelve apostles and the contrast between the kingdom of God and earthly powers. It emphasizes the importance of following Jesus' teachings and prioritizing spiritual growth over worldly duties.

939.summary: The class discusses Jesus calming the storm in Mark 4:35-41, emphasizing Jesus' humanity and the disciples' faith. It also covers Jesus healing the demon-possessed man, highlighting the power of Christ and the joy of salvation.
